correctness.rationale: For complete multipartite graphs, total domination is equivalent to occupying at least two parts. The secure-swap proof exhausts support sizes: support at least three always survives a swap, while support exactly two fails precisely when an omitted vertex must be defended by the sole selected vertex of the opposite occupied part. Inclusion-exclusion of those two obstructions gives the polynomial. The packaged verifier independently checked the graph definition, classification and coefficients on 297 ordered profiles, 87,788 subsets and 2,589 coefficient positions through order 9. The finite replay is only corroboration; the unrestricted claim is proved symbolically.

originality.rationale: The final claim is the all-cardinality classification and enumerator, not the known definition or minimum parameter. Searches across a semantic findings database and the primary literature found minimum/bound work, rooted-product formulas, chain/cograph algorithms, and complete-multipartite cover-pebbling formulas, but no statement implying the displayed enumerator. The closest complete-multipartite full text inspected uses selected secure-total sets only as pebbling witnesses. Full access to the 2007 foundational paper was unavailable, so residual risk is explicitly retained.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete structural classification and every cardinality count for a standard protection invariant on a central graph family containing cliques, stars, complete bipartite graphs and Turán graphs. The polynomial is an exact refinement of the minimum parameter, and the support obstruction is mathematically reusable. Its motivation is intrinsic to the invariant and family rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
